en: The Ritual for the Final Rites (Antyeṣṭividhi).

Now follows the purification of the paths (*adhvaśuddhi*), which is the final rite (*vitāntyeṣṭi*). (p.5b, l.1)

As before, for the purpose of joining the channels (*nāḍī-sandhāna*), one should prepare the binding cord (*pāśasūtra*)— triple-folded and tripled— as in the initiation for Nirvāṇa through the cessation of karma; having equipped it with scissors, washed it with the *astra* mantra, sprinkled it with the *astra*, and protected it with the *kavaca*, one should inform Śiva and, beginning from the big toe up to the crest-lock, bind [the cord] with the root mantra.

In that [channel] consisting of Suṣumnā, one should say: "Oṃ lūṃ, salutation to Suṣumnā. Thus, having integrated Suṣumnā through the unification of Iḍā and Piṅgalā, having joined it to the thread, worshipped it, and performed the ritual binding (avakuṇṭhana), one should offer three oblations for the sake of its presence.
Then, having worshipped the Śakti on the head of the disciple with her own mantra, one should take hold of it.

Having joined [the disciple] with the thread, honored him, and enveloped him for the sake of his presence, one should offer three oblations. Having sprinkled the disciple on the heart with the *astra* mantra—
[reciting] "Oṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ"— one should separate him by means of the *jyeṣṭhā* [mudrā] and strike him with a flower.

Having emerged from oneself through the *recaka* [exhalation] with the syllable *huṃ*, and having entered that [self] into the heart by means of the left channel (*vāmanāḍī*) through the *pūraka* [inhalation], one should contemplate that consciousness—which has the form of a shimmering star—as residing within the seed-syllable *haṃ*.
[Then recite: *oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ svāhā*.
Having drawn [the soul] upward with the *aṅkuśa-mudrā*, having led it to the *dvādaśānta*,
and having contemplated the individual soul (*jīva*) in the form of a drop on the tip of a blade of grass, one should grasp it with the *saṃhāra-mudrā* using the *ātma-mantra*.
Then, by means of the inhalation (*pūraka*), having placed it in its own location starting from the heart, one should perform the retention (*kumbhaka*).

Recalling the root mantra, having led [the self] to one's own *dvādaśānta* by means of the *ātman-mantra* through the sequence of abandoning the causal deities beginning with Brahmā, and having grasped it;
then, having brought it to the space between the eyebrows by way of emanation (*sṛṣṭi*), and having expelled it through the exhaling breath (*recaka*) of the right channel of the self;
joining it to the thread with the mantra "oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ ātmane namaḥ," one should contemplate it as all-pervading and perform the ritual sealing (*avakuṇṭhana*).
One should offer three oblations with the root mantra for the *sannidhāna* offering.
Then, one should offer [oblations] for the three bonds (*pāśa*) of impurity (*mala*), action (*karman*), and illusion (*māyā*) with the root mantra. Following that:
*oṃ hāṃ namo bhoktṛtvakāraṇāya malapāśāya*.

Thus, having meditated on that form of darkness: "Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the *laukikā* bonds of worldly action, which are the causes for the experience of pleasure and pain"—thus [meditate on] those of white and black forms. "Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the bond of *māyā*, the cause of the body, the senses, and their objects"—thus [meditate on] those of various colors. "Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Śiva-śakti, the presiding deity of the bonds"—thus, having meditated on that form of darkness.

Taking [the element] from the body of the disciple, *namaḥ*; having joined it to that which resides in the thread (*sūtra*), having worshipped it, and having brought it into proximity, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra and observe the *nivṛtti-kalā*. () *oṃ hāṃ* to the Earth-element, *namaḥ*, once. *oṃ hāṃ* to Bhadrakālī, *namaḥ*. To Vīrabhadra, *namaḥ*.

Having thus beheld the *nivṛttikalā* which contains the principles (*tattva*) and so forth, one should strike below the knee with a flower while reciting: *oṃ hlāṃ nivṛttikalāyai haḥ hūṃ phaṭ*.
Then, having gathered it in with the *saṃhāramudrā* during inhalation (*pūraka*), one should say: *oṃ hlāṃ nivṛttikalāyai namaḥ*.
Having joined [the mantras] in the place of the *nivṛtti-kalā*, one should worship them, veil them (*avakuṇṭhya*), and offer three oblations (*āhuti*) for the sake of their presence (*sannidhāna*).
Thereafter, one should gaze [upon them] with the mantra: "Aṃ Hvīṃ, obeisance to the *pratiṣṭhā*-kalā.
Then: "Oṃ Hāṃ, obeisance to the *prakṛti-tattva*; obeisance to the *guṇa-tattva*; obeisance to the *buddhi-tattva*."

"Salutation to the one whose quality is resonance"—thus [is] the quality (*guṇa*). "Salutation to the white-colored one"—thus [is] the color (*varṇa*). "Salutation to the one with a circular form"—(line 8)—thus [is] the mandala (*maṇḍala*).
"Salutation to the state beyond the fourth"—thus [is] the state (*avasthā*).

Having meditated upon the *kalā* Beyond Peace (*śāntyatīta*) together with these; or else—
"Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Śāntyatīta-kalā who is pregnant with the essence of the principles (tattva), worlds (bhuvana), phonemes (varṇa), words (pada), and mantras"—having thus beheld her;

[one should say] "Oṃ hauṃ, huṃ phaṭ to the Śāntyatīta-kalā," and having struck [her] below the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra) with a flower, one should take [her] in by means of the inhalation (pūraka) and the withdrawal gesture (saṃhāramudrā). "Oṃ hauṃ, obeisance to the Śāntyatīta-kalā."

Having thus joined the thread from the top-knot (*cūḍā*) to the forehead (*lalāṭa*), one should worship it. Having wound it around, one should offer three oblations (*āhuti*) for the sake of its presence.
In this manner, having gratified [the deity] with three oblations at a time, ending each with "svāhā," in due order—
Oṃ hrūṃ hlāṃ hrūṃ, to the *nivṛtti-kalā*, haḥ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ hrūṃ hviṃ hrūṃ, to the *pratiṣṭhā-kalā*, haḥ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ hrūṃ hrūṃ hrūṃ, to the *vidyā-kalā*, haḥ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ hrūṃ hyaiṃ hrūṃ śāntikalāyai haḥ hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ hrūṃ haḥ hrūṃ śāntyatītakalāyai haḥ hūṃ phaṭ. Thus, the kindling is performed with three oblations for each.

Having smeared with saffron and other substances the locations for the threads at the knees, navel, throat, between the eyebrows, and the *brahmarandhra*, and having worshipped Śiva together with his limbs (*sāṅga*) therein;
[one should then] strike the thread below the knee, along with flowers, using the *nārāca-mudrā* while reciting: *oṃ haḥ astrāya huṃ phaṭ*.

Having entered with "oṃ hrūṃ hlāṃ hrūṃ" and having grasped [the thread], one should offer three oblations with that same mantra ending in "svāhā. Then, one should tie knots in the thread with: "oṃ hauṃ hlāṃ, O Blessed One, bind, bind the pervasive [principles] beginning with the bond of the nivṛtti-kalā, the impurities, karma, māyā-śakti, the tattvas, and the worlds—huṃ phaṭ!"
Having struck the navel-sūtra with flowers using the weapon-mantra (*astra*) and the *nārāca* mudrā,
one enters with the mantra "Oṃ hūṃ, obeisance to the digit of consecration (*pratiṣṭhākalā*)," takes hold [of it],
and offers three oblations ending with "svāhā."

"Oṃ hauṃ hvīṃ hauṃ, [you who are] the *pratiṣṭhā* aspect, pervading the bonds (*pāśa*), impurities (*mala*), karma, the power of *māyā*, the principles (*tattva*), the worlds (*bhuvana*), and so forth—bind, bind! Huṃ phaṭ! With these words, one should tie knots in the thread.
Afterwards, having struck the neck-thread with flowers using the *nārāca-mudrā* and the weapon-mantra (*astra*), [one should proceed].

Having entered with "Oṃ hrūṃ, obeisance to Vidyākalā" and taken hold [of the thread], one should offer three oblations ending in "svāhā. Then, one should tie knots in the thread with: "Oṃ hauṃ hrūṃ hauṃ, bind, bind the noose of Vidyākalā, the impurity of karma, the power of Māyā, and that which pervades the principles, worlds, and so forth; huṃ phaṭ!"
Thereafter—
having struck the forehead region with the *nārāca* mudrā while reciting "Oṃ haḥ hūṃ phaṭ" over a thread adorned with flowers,
and having entered by reciting "Oṃ hyeṃ śāntikalāyai namaḥ," one should take hold [of it] and offer three oblations with that same [mantra], ending in *svāhā*.

Oṃ hauṃ hyaiṃ hauṃ—[one should recite] "bind, bind, huṃ phaṭ," which pervades the impurities, karma, the power of māyā, the principles (tattva), the worlds (bhuvana), and so forth; with this, one should make knots in the thread.
Then, having struck the thread on the head with flowers using the weapon-mantra (astra) and the nārāca-mudrā.
Having entered with "Oṃ hauṃ, obeisance to Śāntikalā," and having taken [the vessel], he offers three oblations ending in svāhā. Then:
"Oṃ hauṃ hvīṃ hauṃ, O Blessed One, [to] the bond of the Śāntyatīta-kalā, [and its] impure karma, māyā-śakti, tattva, world-spheres (bhuvana), and so forth..."
One should make knots in the thread with the mantra: *vyāpakaṃ bandha bandha huṃ phaṭ*.
In this interval, for the sake of liberation from sins such as forgetfulness, one should offer a hundred oblations (*āhuti*) with the root mantra (*mūla*).
Then, having worshipped the Support Power (*ādhāraśakti*) in the fire and offered three oblations—
In the body of the disciple’s thread, below the knees, in the location of the *nivṛtti-kalā*, one should contemplate its pervasion:
*oṃ hlāṃ nivṛttikalāyai namaḥ*. *oṃ hāṃ pṛthvī-tattvāya namaḥ*.
*kālāgnirudrāya namaḥ*. *kūṣmāṇḍāya namaḥ*.

Salutation to the *puṃgāndharva* womb; salutation to the *aindra* womb; salutation to the *saumya* womb;
salutation to the *prājeśa* womb; salutation to the *brahma* womb—thus are the fourteen wombs (*yonis*).
Having visualized the *nivṛtti-kalā* as being permeated by all of these;
or else, having visualized it with: *oṃ hlāṃ, obeisance to the Nivṛtti-kalā which contains the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), and mantras*.
Oṃ hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ nivṛttikalāyai haḥ hūṃ phaṭ—having thus struck below the knee with a flower;
Oṃ hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ nivṛttikalāyai svāhā—having drawn [the deity] in by means of the inhalation (*pūraka*) and the hook-gesture (*aṅkuśamudrā*);
Oṃ hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ nivṛttikalāyai hūṃ phaṭ—having grasped [it] by means of the retention (*kumbhaka*) and the withdrawal-gesture (*saṃhāramudrā*).

"Oṃ hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Nivṛttikalā"— with this, by means of the exhalation (*recaka*) and the *utthānamudrā*, one should establish [the deity] within the *kuṇḍa* upon the Śakti who is the support (*ādhārarūpiṇī*).
Having worshipped with "Oṃ hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Nivṛttikalā" and offered the *arghya*,

and having offered three oblations (*āhuti*) ending in *svāhā* for the purpose of invoking the presence (*sannidhāna*), one should contemplate the three bonds (*pāśatraya*)— consisting of *mala*, *karman*, and *māyā*— which produce the state of being an enjoyer (*bhoktṛtva*), the body of experience (*bhoga-śarīra*), and so forth.
Thereafter, having invoked Brahmā with "Oṃ hāṃ brahmaṇe namaḥ" and worshipped him,
and having offered three oblations for his presence (*sannidhāna*), one should inform him and visualize infinite wombs (*yoni*) within that digit (*kalā*).
Then, having invoked Vāgīśī and Vāgīśa who pervade it, and having worshipped them, one offers three oblations for their presence.
Having requested, "May the two Blessed Ones be present for the sake of favoring the sacrificial animal," and having sprinkled the disciple with the *astra* mantra,
one should strike him in the region of the heart with the *sapuṣpa-nārāca-mudrā* while reciting "oṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ. Then,
entering his body through the exhalation (*recaka*) of oneself by means of the syllable *huṃ*, one should separate [the soul] from it using the *jyeṣṭhā* finger while reciting "oṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ."

Reciting "Oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ svāhā," having drawn [the vital breath] upward with the *aṅkuśa-mudrā* while recollecting the root mantra, one should lead it to the *dvādaśānta*. Having visualized the *jīva* in the form of a drop on the tip of a blade of grass, one should grasp it with the *saṃhāra-mudrā*, saying: "Oṃ hūṃ haṃ hāṃ huṃ, obeisance to the Self. Then, having placed it within one's own heart by means of the previously mentioned [mudrā] and performed *kumbhaka*, one should again recollect the root mantra: "Oṃ hūṃ haṃ hāṃ huṃ, obeisance to the Self."

Having led [the self] to one's own *dvādaśānta* by means of the sequential abandonment of the causes beginning with Brahmā, and having gathered it back and expelled it according to the previously mentioned sequence, one should visualize the union of the parents. With the *udbhavamudrā* of the left hand, reciting "Oṃ hūṃ haṃ hāṃ huṃ, obeisance to the Self," one should effect the simultaneous union of the Self in all wombs in the form of the *pūraka* breath-retention. Having worshipped with the root mantra, three oblations (*āhuti*) should be offered. One should then request: "O Blessed One, grant the simultaneous union of this Self in all wombs; grant it! Thus he should inform [the deity].

Then, for the sake of the completion of all the embryos, having offered three oblations with the root mantra, [one should pray]: "O Blessed One, effect the simultaneous completion of the embryos of this self within all wombs; do, do! Then, for the sake of birth, having performed three oblations with the root mantra, [one should pray]: "O Blessed One, effect the birth of all these embryos of this self; do, do!"

Then, for the sake of empowerment, having conceived the simultaneous growth of all bodies and having meditated upon the accumulation of karma that brings about various enjoyments within bodies of all origins, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra, saying: "O Blessed One, perform the accumulation of karma that brings about various enjoyments for this self."

Thereafter, due to the differences of place, time, body, and object, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra, having mentally gathered within the self—the *liṅga*—the experience (*bhoga*) consisting of the sensation of pleasure and pain, which is the state of being an enjoyer (*bhoktṛtva*), acquired through the exhaustion of past karma, and appearing in various forms.
One should inform [the deity], saying: "O Blessed One, effect the accomplishment of the enjoyment of this self everywhere. One should thus make the request.

In the interval [between initiations], during the initiation for the deceased (*mṛtakadīkṣā*), one should perform the forty purificatory rites (*saṃskāra*)—beginning with conception (*garbhādhāna*) and ending with the naming (*nāmadheya*)—in the world of earth (*bhūloka*) by means of oblations of clarified butter (*ghṛtāhuti*) in groups of three.

These are as follows: conception (*garbhādhāna*); the rite for a male child (*puṃsavana*); the parting of the hair (*sīmanta*); the offering to Viṣṇu (*viṣṇubali*); the birth-rite (*jātakarma*); the naming (*nāmakaraṇa*);

the first outing (*upaniṣkrāmaṇa*); the first feeding of solid food (*annaprāśana*); the tonsure (*caula*); the initiation (*upanayana*); and the four Vedic vows (*vedavrata*): the *aiṣṭika*, the *dārvika*, the *bhautika*, and the *sautika*.

The gift of a cow; the offering of morsels of food from the hand; the *śrāddha* on the occasion of the *aṣṭakā* festival; the *śrāvaṇī*; the *āgrayaṇī*; the *caitrī*; the *āśvayujī*; the seven-fold forest of Maghā; the establishment of the sacred fires (*ādhāna*); the fire-oblation (*agnihotra*); the new- and full-moon sacrifices (*darśapūrṇamāsa*); the full-moon sacrifice (*paurṇamāsa*); the four-monthly sacrifice (*cāturmāsya*);
the animal sacrifice (*paśubandha*); the *sautrāmaṇī* rite; the offerings of oblations during the Maghā constellation; the *agniṣṭoma*; the *ukthya*; the *ṣoḍaśī*; and the *vājapeya*.
The Atirātra; the Aptoryāma; the Soma-aghāṭavi; (l. 3) the Aśvamedha; the Vānaprastha; the Parivrājya;

and the Antyeṣṭi, which is included within compassion and so forth. (l. 4) [The following] are the eleven excellent [qualities]: the feet, skin, womb, marrow, bones, private parts, spleen, navel, palate, tongue, ears, eyes, gold, and so on; as well as lack of malice, freedom from envy, tranquility, and purity.

If these qualities of the self— freedom from censure and lack of exertion— are present, one should bring about these obstacles and withdraw them by means of three oblations with the heart-mantra (*hṛdaya*). Thereafter,
having contemplated dissolution (*laya*) in the form of supreme delight toward objects of enjoyment, one should offer three oblations with the root-mantra (*mūla*), and having made a formal request,
one should offer three oblations with the root-mantra for the purification of the channels (*srotas*).

Even when the ritual action has been performed, for the sake of ensuring that [the deity] does not fail to grant the respective results, one should offer three oblations with the heart-mantra (*hṛdaya*) once the reality of cessation has been purified.
Having offered one hundred oblations with the root-mantra (*mūla*) along with the heart-mantra for the purpose of atonement, one should make a formal request.

In the absence of enjoyment (*bhoga*), having conceived the distinction consisting of the outward departure from the bond of *māyā*, one should offer ten oblations with the root mantra of Pāśupata. Having contemplated the effect of impurity (*mala*) in the form of attachment to the state of being an enjoyer (*bhoktṛtva*), one should offer one hundred oblations with the root mantra of Pāśupata for the sake of its cessation. Having conceived the separation from impurity, one should again offer three oblations with the root mantra in the same manner. Then, having conceived the absolute non-existence of *karman*...
Having offered three oblations with the root mantra, one should request:
"O Blessed One, effect the severance—effect the severance—of these three bonds of this self, which consist of impurity, karma, and māyā.
Thereafter, with a blade consecrated by the Astra-mantra recited six times—

Reciting the mantra *oṃ hauṃ hlāṃ hauṃ nivṛttikalāpāśāya haḥ huṃ phaṭ*, one should sever the bond of the *nivṛtti-kalā* at its root with the *astra-mantra* while pronouncing the vowels. Having cut it and cast it away, one should form it into a circle, place it upon a sacrificial ladle (*sruc*) filled with clarified butter (*ājya*), and offer it into the fire with that same mantra.

One should burn it until it is reduced to ashes by offering three oblations of the *astra-mantra* alone. Then, one should inform [the deity]: "O Blessed One, perform the severing of this soul's bond of the *nivṛtti-kalā*—perform it!"

Again, for the sake of removing the sprouts of the noose (*pāśa*), one should offer five oblations with the *astra-mantra* ending in *huṃ phaṭ*. Then, for the purpose of expiation (*prāyaścitta*), having offered eight oblations with the *astra-mantra*, and having contemplated the destruction of the remaining body and the unity of consciousness (*caitanya*), one should invoke and worship Brahmā and offer three oblations.
For the purification of the *puryaṣṭaka*, while uttering "Oṃ Hāṃ," one should offer three oblations with the mantra "Accept sound, touch, and the trident, Svāhā! and then make this request:

"O, O Brahmā! You must ensure that the path to the state free from affliction remains unobstructed; such is the command of the Supreme Goddess. Having thus dismissed Brahmā, and having meditated upon the Self—residing at the summit of the pure principle (*śuddhatattva*), resembling a pure crystal gem, and liberated from the bond of the *nivṛtti-kalā*—he should offer three oblations with the root mantra for the purpose of extraction (*uddhāra*).

(OM HĀṂ HAṂ HĀṂ ĀTMANE NAMAḤ). Having thus extracted the Raudra-self from the fire by means of the Saṃhāriṇī [mudrā], and having brought that self— which resembles the lunar orb released from Rāhu— into the heart of the self by means of the inhalation (*pūraka*) of the left [nostril], and having placed it as before at the *dvādaśānta*,

one should join it to the thread of the disciple’s body by means of the exhalation (*recaka*) and the Udbhava-mudrā, and having performed worship, one should offer a drop of water for the *arghya* with the root mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ* for the purpose of nourishment.

Placing [the vessel] upon the head, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra for the sake of stabilization. Having worshipped the two parents and offered water for the feet (*arghya*) after satisfying them with three oblations, one should perform the full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) with the root mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ*. This is the purification of the *nivṛtti-kalā*.
Thereafter, the joining of the *kalās* (*kalā-sandhāna*) should be performed: having worshipped with "Oṃ hvāṃ hvīṃ, obeisance to Nivṛtti and Pratiṣṭhā," one should satisfy them with three oblations.

Having conceived that the pure [element] is dissolved within the impure, one should establish the power of *pratiṣṭhā*. Then, having worshipped the power of retention (*adhāra-śakti*) in the fire and offered three oblations, one should contemplate its pervasion within the body of the thread at the site of installation.
*Oṃ hāṃ namaḥ to the power of pratiṣṭhā*. *Oṃ hāṃ namaḥ to the water principle (*aptattva*); namaḥ to the fire principle (*tejastattva*).

Salutation to the qualities of taste, form, touch, and sound—these are the qualities.
"Salutation to the object of taste"—this is the *viṣaya* (object).
"Salutation to Viṣṇu, the Lord of Causes"—this is the *kāraṇeśa* (Lord of Causes).

"Salutation to the state of dream"—thus [is] the state.
Having thus meditated upon the kalā of *pratiṣṭhā*, which contains all these [elements] within its womb.

Alternatively—(l.3) one should gaze [upon it] while reciting: *oṃ hvīṃ namas to the kalā of establishment (pratiṣṭhākalā), which contains within it the principles (tattva), worlds (bhuvana), phonemes (varṇa), words (pada), and mantras*.
(l.4) Then, having struck it with a flower while reciting: *oṃ hvīṃ pratiṣṭhākalāyai haḥ huṃ phaṭ*.

"Oṃ hāṃ hvīṃ hāṃ pratiṣṭhākalāyai svāhā"—having drawn [the deity] in with the *pūraka* breath while forming the *aṅkuśa-mudrā*; "Oṃ hauṃ hāṃ hvīṃ hāṃ hauṃ pratiṣṭhākalāyai haḥ huṃ phaṭ"—having gathered [the deity] in with the *kumbhaka* breath while forming the *saṃhāra-mudrā*;
"Oṃ hāṃ hvīṃ hāṃ pratiṣṭhākalāyai namaḥ"—[one should perform this] with the *recaka* breath while forming the *udbhava-mudrā*.

One should place [the deity] into the vessel (*kuṇḍa*), which is the form of the support for power (*śakti*). Having worshipped with "Oṃ hāṃ hvīṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the digit of establishment (*pratiṣṭhākalā*)," and having offered the water of honor (*arghya*), one should offer three oblations (*āhuti*) with the suffix *svāhā* for the sake of presence (*sannidhāna*).
Then, one should contemplate the three bonds (*pāśatraya*), which consist of the nature of impurity (*mala*), action (*karman*), and illusion (*māyā*).

Having invoked Viṣṇu with "Oṃ hīṃ viṣṇave namaḥ" and worshipped him, one should offer three oblations for his presence (*sannidhāna*). Within that digit (*kalā*), having conceived the infinite [beings] whose source is manifold forms,
one should worship Vāgīśī and Vāgīśa, who pervade it, as before, and offer three oblations for their presence.

Having sprinkled the disciple with the weapon-mantra (*astra*), saying "Oṃ haḥ astrāya hūṃ phaṭ," and having struck the region of his heart with a flower using the *nārāca* mudrā, one enters his body with the syllable *huṃ*. Then, with the *jyeṣṭhā* [finger], one separates [the consciousness] with "Oṃ huṃ hāṃ huṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ.

Next, drawing it upward with the *aṅkuśa* mudrā while reciting "Oṃ huṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ huṃ svāhā," and while recollecting the root mantra, one leads it to the *dvādaśānta* (the twelve-finger space above the head).

Having visualized the individual soul (*jīva*) as being like a drop on the tip of a blade of grass, and having gathered it together with the *ātma-mantra* by means of the *saṃhāra-mudrā*, one should place it within one's own heart through the process of inhalation (*pūraka*).

Then, performing retention (*kumbhaka*) while recollecting the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*), one should lead it to one's own *dvādaśānta* by means of the *ātma-mantra* through the sequence of abandoning the causal layers. Finally, one should contemplate the union of the parents.
Having performed a simultaneous union with oneself in the form of the manifestation of all wombs (*yonis*) by means of the *vāmā* and *udbhava* mudrās and the recitation of one’s own mantra;

having worshipped with the root mantra and offered three oblations (*āhuti*), and having made a formal request; [one should] offer three oblations with the root mantra for the sake of the completion of all embryos.
Having made the request; having offered three oblations with the *prāsāda* mantra for the sake of their union (*sandhāna*) and having made the request;

having offered three oblations with the root mantra (*mūla*) for the sake of authority (*adhikāra*) and having made the request; having offered three oblations with the root mantra for the sake of gain (*lābha*) and having made the request; having offered three oblations with the root mantra for the purification of the stream (*srotas*) and having made the request [for the sake] of the rite (*karman*).

For the sake of the power of procreation (*prasavitva*), for the cause, and for the purification of the state of establishment (*pratiṣṭhātatvaśuddhau*), one should perform three heart-oblations (*hṛdāhuti*).

For the purpose of expiation (*niṣkṛti*), having offered a hundred oblations with the root mantra together with the head-mantra (*saśirasāmūlena*), [one should pray]: "O Blessed One, through this expiation of myself, after initiation, please effect the complete purification of my ritual actions (*sakarma*) caused by any deficiency in conduct (*ācāravaikalyanimitta*) regarding what was desired."

Having visualized the separation in the form of emerging outside the noose of *māyā* by [uttering] "Do it!", one should offer a hundred oblations with the root mantra along with the *Pāśupata* [mantra]. Then, for the purpose of obstructing the impurity (*mala*), having likewise offered ten oblations with the root mantra and resolved upon the separation from the impurity, one should again offer three oblations with the root mantra in the same manner. [This is done] even for one who is devoted to ritual action (*karman*).

Having conceptualized the separation as having the nature of an existent entity, and having again offered three oblations with the root mantra, one should inform [the deity]: "O Blessed One, effect the separation of these three bonds of this self, which consist of the impurity of *māyā* and karma; do it, do it!
This should be performed seven times while reciting the weapon-mantra (*astra*). [The mantra is: *oṃ hāṃ hvīṃ hāṃ pratiṣṭhākalā pāśāya haḥ huṃ phaṭ*.

With this mantra, having performed the rite of consecration (*pratiṣṭhākalā*) with its proper sound, having severed [the bonds] at the limit of the fetters (*pāśa*), having released them with the *astra* mantra, and having rolled [the object] into a ball, one should place it upon a blade of *kūrcagrass* filled with ghee; then, having offered oblations together with clarified butter using that same mantra, one should burn it.
With the *astra* mantra alone, by means of three oblations, one should reduce it to ashes.
Having requested the Blessed One to perform the severing of the bonds of the kalās that constitute his own self,
and having again offered five oblations with the weapon-mantra ending in *huṃ phaṭ* for the cessation of the sprouts of the bonds,
he offers eight oblations with the weapon-mantra for the sake of expiation.
Having contemplated the oneness of consciousness with the destruction of the remaining body, having invoked Viṣṇu and begun the worship, and having offered three oblations; then,
for the sake of purifying the *puryaṣṭaka*, having offered three oblations with the mantra "Oṃ hāṃ, O Viṣṇu, accept this pure [oblation], svāhā," one should make the formal request.
"O Viṣṇu, you must create an obstruction for this one who is proceeding to the state free from affliction; such is the supreme command of the Goddess. Thus one should dismiss Viṣṇu.
In this manner, one should [visualize] the Self as situated at the tip of the pure principle (*śuddhatattva*), resembling a pure crystal gem, and liberated from the network of the *pratiṣṭhā* kalās.
Having reflected thus, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra for the sake of extraction (*uddhāra*).
Having informed the fierce self (*raudrātmāna*) and grasped it with the *saṃhāriṇī* [mudrā], one should draw it out from the fire.

Then, by means of the left nostril and inhalation (*pūraka*), having brought the self—resembling a half-moon released from Rāhu—into the heart, one should [draw it out] with exhalation (*recaka*) using the *udbhava-mudrā*.

Having joined the disciple to the body of the Sūtra and worshipped him, one should offer a drop of arghya water upon his head with the root mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ* for the sake of nourishment; then, having offered three oblations with the root mantra for the purpose of stabilization,
one should thereafter worship the two parents, offer three oblations, and present them with arghya.
Having offered the full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) with the root mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ*, this is the purification of the *pratiṣṭhā*-kala.

Having uttered the short vowel for the pure *pratiṣṭhā*-kala, one should utter the long vowel for the pure *vidyā*-kala. Then, having worshipped with "Oṃ hvīṃ hrūṃ, obeisance to Pratiṣṭhā and Vidyā," one should offer three oblations.
Having contemplated that the pure [principle] is merged within the impure, one should bring forth the *vidyā-kalā*.
Having worshipped with "Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Support-Power (*ādhāraśakti*)," and having offered three oblations,
one should contemplate its pervasion within the body of the thread at the locus of *vidyā*.
"Oṃ hrūṃ, homage to the category of knowledge (vidyākalā)," thus one should gaze.

(l. 7) "Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the principle of the person (puruṣatattva); homage to the principle of passion (rāgatattva); homage to the principle of necessity (niyatitattva); homage to the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva); homage to the principle of limited agency (kalātattva); homage to the principle of time (kālatattva)."
Salutation to the principle of Māyā—thus are the seven principles.
Salutation to Vāmā. Salutation to Bhīmā. Salutation to Ugrā. Salutation to Bhava. Salutation to Īśāna. Salutation to Ekavīra.
Salutation to Pracaṇḍa. Salutation to Umāpati. (l. 3) Salutation to Aja.
Salutation to Ananta. Salutation to Ekaśiva. Salutation to Krodheśa. Salutation to Caṇḍa. (l. 4) Salutation to Jyotis. Salutation to Saṃvarta.
Homage to Śūra. Homage to Pañcāntaka. (l. 5) Homage to Ekavīra. Homage to Śikheda. Homage to Mahādyuti. (l. 6) Homage to Vāmadeva.
Homage to Bhava. Homage to Udbhava. Homage to Ekapiṅgala. (l. 7)
Salutation to Ekekṣaṇa. Salutation to Īśāna. Salutation to Aṅguṣṭhamātra—these are the twenty-seven worlds. (l. 8) Salutation to Jña-kāra. Salutation to Jha-kāra. Salutation to Ja-kāra.
Salutation to Cha-kāra. (l. 9) Salutation to Ca-kāra. Salutation to Ña-kāra.
Salutation to the letter *gha*—thus are the seven syllables.

(p. 36b, l. 1) Salutation to the Pervasive One, O Pervasive One! Salutation to the Sky-like One, O Sky-like One! Salutation to the Conscious and the Unconscious! (l. 2) Salutation to the Supreme Lord! Salutation to the one whose form is light!

Homage to the one presiding over all yogas. Homage to the lord of all vidyās. Homage to the one who is without end. Homage to the protector. Homage to the secret of secrets. Oṃ, homage, homage! Homage to the form of Sadyojāta. Homage to the secret of Vāmadeva. Homage to the heart of Aghora.

Salutation to the one whose face is the Tatpuruṣa; salutation to the Īśāna-head; salutation to Śiva; salutation to the source of all; *oṃ* salutation to Śiva—these are twenty words. *Oṃ hrūṃ*, salutation to the Śikhā; *oṃ huṃ*, salutation to the Aghora-heart—these are two mantras.
Homage to the letter *ma*. Homage to the letter *ra*—these are the two seed-syllables (*bīja*).
Homage to the hand and tongue. Homage to Alampuṣā—these are the two channels (*nāḍī*). Homage to knowledge (*jñāna*). Homage to Nāga—these are the two winds (*vāyu*).
Salutation to the foot-faculty. Salutation to the razor-faculty—these are the two faculties.
Salutation to the object of form—this is the object.
Salutation to the qualities of form, touch, and sound—these are the qualities.

"Salutation to Rudra, the Lord of Causes"—thus [is] the Lord of Causes. "Salutation to the one of red color"—thus [is] the color. "Salutation to the mandala adorned with a svastika"—thus [is] the mandala.
"Salutation to the state of deep sleep"—thus [is] the state. (l.
7) With all these [elements], one should contemplate the Vidyā-kalā as being pregnant [with them].
(l. 8) Or else, having observed: "Oṃ hrūṃ, salutation to the Vidyā-kalā pregnant with the principles (tattva), worlds (bhuvana), phonemes (varṇa), words (pada), and mantras. (p. 37b, l. 1)
OṂ HĀṂ HRŪṂ HĀṂ VIDYĀKALĀYAI HAḤ HUMPHAṬ— having thus struck with a flower below the *ghalā*,
OṂ HĀṂ HRŪṂ HĀṂ VIDYĀKALĀYAI SVĀHĀ— having drawn it up by means of the inhalation (*pūraka*) and the hook-gesture (*aṅkuśamudrā*),
OṂ HAUṂ HĀṂ HRŪṂ HĀṂ HAUṂ VIDYĀKALĀYAI HAḤ HUMPHAṬ— having seized it by means of the retention (*kumbhaka*) and the withdrawal-gesture (*saṃhāramudrā*).

(1.6) *Oṃ hāṃ huṃ hāṃ vidyākalāyai namaḥ*. With this [mantra] and the *rocaka* [mudrā], along with the *udbhava-mudrā*, one should establish [the deity] within the *kuṇḍa* upon the Śakti who is the form of the support.
(1.7–8) Having worshipped her with *oṃ hāṃ huṃ hāṃ vidyākalāyai namaḥ* and having offered the *arghya*, [one should proceed]. (p.38a, 1.1)

Having offered three oblations ending with "svāhā," one should contemplate the three bonds— consisting of *mala*, *karman*, and *māyā*— which produce the state of being an enjoyer (*bhoktṛtva*), the objects of enjoyment, the body, and so forth. Thereafter—
Having invoked Rudra and worshipped him, one should offer three oblations for his presence.

Within that *kalā*, having visualized infinite sources of various forms, one should worship Vāgīśī and Vāgīśa—who pervade it—as before, offering three oblations for their presence. Then, having sprinkled the disciple with the *astra-mantra*, [one should strike] the region of the heart with the *sapuṣpa-nārāca-mudrā* while reciting: *oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ*.

Having struck [the disciple] with one's own *recaka* breath, one enters his body with the syllable *huṃ*. Then, having separated [the soul] by means of the *jyeṣṭhā* [mudrā] while reciting *oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ*, and having drawn it upward with the *aṅkuśa-mudrā* while reciting *oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ svāhā*, one should—while recollecting the root mantra—lead it to the *dvādaśānta*. Having visualized the *jīva* in the form of a drop on the tip of a blade of grass, one should grasp it with the *saṃhāra-mudrā* while reciting *oṃ huṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ huṃ ātmane namaḥ*, and having established it in one’s own heart through the function of *pūraka*, one should perform *kumbhaka*.

Recalling the root mantra—*oṃ hūṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ hūṃ ātmane namaḥ*—and having led [the self] to one's own *dvādaśānta* by means of the sequence of abandoning the causal deities beginning with Brahmā, one should expel it through the right channel (*dakṣiṇanāḍī*). Having meditated upon the union of the parents, one should effect the simultaneous union of the self with all wombs (*sarvayoni*) in the form of manifold manifestations through the left channel using the *udbhavamudrā*, while reciting: *oṃ hūṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ hūṃ ātmane namaḥ*. Then, having worshipped with the root mantra and offered three oblations (*āhuti*), one should make a formal request (*vijñāpayet*).

Then, having offered three oblations with the *mūla-mantra* for the purpose of generation (*janana*), and having made a formal request; (l. 3) having meditated upon the simultaneous growth of all bodies for the sake of empowerment (*adhikāra*); (l. 4) and having contemplated the cleansing of karma that brings about experience within all bodies born from various wombs; (l. 5) having offered three oblations with the *mūla-mantra*, and having made a formal request; (l. 6) having reflected upon the nature of the experiencer (*bhoktṛtva*)—which, though appearing in manifold forms due to differences of place, time, body, and object, consists essentially of the sensation of pleasure and pain—within the self that possesses the subtle body (*liṅgin*); (l. 7–8) having offered three oblations with the *mūla-mantra*.

Having made the request regarding the objects of enjoyment, one should contemplate absorption (*laya*) in the form of supreme delight and offer three oblations with the root mantra. Having made the request, for the purification of the streams that consist of the continuous flow of the activities of *māyā*, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra. Having made the request, for the sake of purifying the principle of knowledge (*vidyā-tattva*) so that the power of action (*karman*) may no longer produce [rebirth] and is destroyed, one should perform three oblations with the heart-mantra (*hṛdaya*). For the purpose of expiation (*niṣkṛti*), having offered one hundred oblations with the root mantra preceded by the crest-mantra (*śikhā*), [this is done] as an expiation for oneself before the Blessed One.

Having requested, "Perform the complete purification of all karma," and having distinguished [the soul] from the noose of *māyā*, he should offer three oblations with the root mantra and the *pāśupata* mantra. Then, for the cessation of impurity (*mala*), he should likewise offer one hundred oblations. Having resolved upon the separation from impurity, he should again offer three oblations with the root mantra. He should then request, "Perform the distinction of the three nooses of the Blessed One and of myself—consisting of *māyā*, impurity, and karma. Following that, [he should perform the cutting] seven times with a blade over which the weapon mantra has been recited.

Oṃ hāṃ huṃ hāṃ, [reciting] "to the noose of the *vidyākalā*—haḥ hūṃ phaṭ," one should sever it at its very root with the *astra-mantra*, cast it away, and having rolled it into a ball, place it upon the sacrificial grass (*sṛc*) in the *vratapūrṇā* vessel. Then, having offered oblations of clarified butter (*ājya*) together with that same mantra, one should burn it. One should reduce it to ashes with three oblations of the *astra-mantra* alone. Having requested the Blessed One, saying "Act, act! [to sever] the binding of the *vidyākalā* noose for myself," one should again offer five oblations with the *astra-mantra* ending in *hūṃ phaṭ* for the cessation of the sprout of the noose.

Having offered eight oblations with the *astra-mantra* for the sake of expiation (*prāyaścitta*), one should contemplate the unity of the remaining body and consciousness. Having invoked Rudra, worshipped him, and offered three oblations, one should offer three oblations for the purification of the *puryaṣṭaka* (the eightfold city), saying: "Oṃ Hāṃ! O Rudra, accept this fragrant fee (*gandha-śulka*); Svāhā! Then, one should address him as follows: "O Rudra, you must provide protection for the path to the state free from affliction for this [deceased] soul; such is the command of the Supreme Goddess. Thus, one should dismiss Rudra.

Having meditated upon the Self as abiding in the supreme purity, resembling a pure crystal gem, and liberated from the net of *vidyā* and *kalā*, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra for the purpose of extraction (*uddhāra*). Having made this request— saying "Oṃ huṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ huṃṃ, obeisance to the Self"— one should extract the Self from the fire by means of the *raudrī* [mudrā] and the left nostril during inhalation (*apūraka*), using the *saṃhāriṇī* [mudrā].

Having brought his own heart, which resembles the orb of the half-moon released by Rāhu, into [the disciple's body] by means of the *recaka* breath and the *utthāna-mudrā*, and having joined it to the thread of the disciple’s body and worshipped it, one should offer the *arghya* drop on the head with the root mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ* for the purpose of nourishment. Having offered three oblations (*āhuti*) with the root mantra for the sake of stabilization, and having worshipped and offered the *arghya* to the two parents, one should dismiss them. One should give the full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) with the root mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ*. This is the purification of the *vidyā-kalā*.

In this interval, regarding the initiation for one who has died in an improper place (*asthāna-mṛtaka-dīkṣā*), the teachers maintain that one should offer a hundred oblations with the root mantra (*mūla*) for the sake of the absolute severance of the subtle body (*sūkṣmadeha*) and for the cessation of the bondage of impurity (*mala*).
Following that is the reintegration of the *kalās*.

Then, having uttered the short [seed-syllable] of the Pure Vidyā, one should utter the long [syllable] of the Pure Śāntikalā. Having worshipped with "Oṃ huṃ hyaiṃ, obeisance to Vidyā and Śānti," and having offered three oblations ending in svāhā,
one should contemplate the Pure [element] as dissolved into the Impure, and then invoke the Śāntikalā.

One should worship with the mantra "Obeisance to the Support-Power" (*ādhāraśaktaye namaḥ*). Having offered three oblations, one should contemplate its pervasion within the body of the thread at the location of the *śāntikalā*. One should contemplate with the mantra "Oṃ hyaiṃ, obeisance to the *śāntikalā*.

(Then: "Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the principle of Pure Knowledge" (*śuddhavidyā-tattva*); "obeisance to the principle of Īśvara"; "obeisance to the principle of Sadāśiva"—these are the three principles (*tattvas*).

Salutation to Vāmā; salutation to Jyeṣṭhā; salutation to Raudrī; salutation to Kālī; salutation to Kalavīkaraṇī; salutation to Balavikaraṇī; salutation to Balapramathinī; salutation to Sarvabhūtadamanī; salutation to Manonmanī; salutation to Ananta; salutation to Sūkṣma; salutation to Śivottama; salutation to Ekanetra; salutation to Ekarudra; salutation to Trimūrti; salutation to Śrīkaṇṭha.

Salutation to Śikhaṇḍin—(l. 3) thus [are] the seventeen worlds named after the Rudras. Salutation to the world of Sadāśiva—(l. 4) this is one world. Salutation to the letter Ga; salutation to the letter Kha; salutation to the letter Ka—(l. 5) these are the three phonemes.

Salutation to the eternal Yogi. Salutation to him who is seated upon the seat of yoga. (l. 6) Salutation to the everlasting one. Salutation to the firm one. Salutation to the unsupported one. Salutation to the protectorless one.
Salutation to the infinite one. Salutation to Śiva. (l. 7) Salutation to the all-pervading one.

Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the one whose form is space; obeisance to the one who pervades space—these are the eleven words. Obeisance to the armor; obeisance to the face of Tatpuruṣa—these are the two mantras. Obeisance to the bindu; obeisance to the letter ya—these are the two seed-syllables.
Salutation to Yaśā; salutation to Alampuṣā—these are the two channels (*nāḍī*). Salutation to Kūrmā; salutation to Kṛkara—these are the two winds (*vāyu*).
Salutation to the sense of touch (*tvag-indriya*); salutation to the sense of the hand (*pāṇi-indriya*)—these are the two senses (*indriya*).
"Salutation to the object of touch"—this refers to the *viṣaya* (object).
"Salutation to the two qualities of touch and sound"—these refer to the *guṇas* (qualities).
"Salutation to the Lord, the Lord of the instruments"—this refers to the *kāraṇeśa* (Lord of the causes).
"Salutation to the fourth state"—thus [is] the state (*avasthā*).
"Salutation to the black-colored one"—thus [is] the color (*varṇa*).
"Salutation to the maṇḍala adorned with a six-cornered figure and six dots"—thus [is] the maṇḍala (*maṇḍala*).

Therefore, having mentally contemplated the *śāntikalā* as being infused with all of these, or alternatively, having observed: "Oṃ hyaiṃ, obeisance to the *śāntikalā* who contains the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), and mantras," one should strike [the locus] below the midpoint of the eyebrows with a flower, saying: "Oṃ hāṃ hyaiṃ hāṃ śāntikalāyai haḥ huṃ phaṭ."
Saying "Oṃ hāṃ hyai hāṃ śāntikalāyai svāhā," one should attract [the power] by means of the *aṅkuśa-mudrā* and inhalation (*pūraka*).
Saying "Oṃ hauṃ hāṃ hyaiṃ hāṃ hauṃ śāntikalāyai haḥ huṃ phaṭ," one should seize it by means of the *saṃhāra-mudrā* and breath-retention (*kumbhaka*).

Then, saying "Oṃ hāṃ hyaiṃ hāṃ hāṃ śāntikalāyai namaḥ," one should cause it to enter the power of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa-śakti*), which has the form of a support, by means of exhalation (*recaka*) and the *udbhava-mudrā*.
Having worshipped with "Oṃ hāṃ hyaiṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Śāntikalā" (l. 2), and having offered the *arghya*, one should offer three oblations ending with *svāhā*.

One should then contemplate the three bonds (*pāśatraya*), the rite for purifying the impurity of office (*adhikāramala*), that which is the form of Mahāmāyā, the state of being an enjoyer (*bhoktṛtva*), and the generator of the body of experience and so forth (ll. 3–4).
Thereafter—
Having worshipped with "Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Īśvara, the Lord of Causes," and having offered three oblations and made a formal request,
one should conceive of the infinite births in various forms within that *kalā*.
Then, having worshipped Vāgīśī and Vāgīśa, who pervade that [kalā], as before, and having offered three oblations for their presence and consumed [the remainder], [one proceeds].

Having sprinkled the disciple with the weapon-mantra (*astra*), and having struck him in the region of the heart with the *nārāca* mudrā accompanied by flowers while reciting "Oṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ," one should enter his body via the *huṃ* syllable through the single aperture of oneself.
Then, having separated [the disciple] from [his previous state] using the *jyeṣṭhā* [mudrā] while reciting "Oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ."

Saying *oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ svāhā* while drawing [the vital breath] upward with the *aṅkuśa-mudrā*, and while recollecting the root mantra, one should lead it to the *dvādaśānta*. Having visualized the *jīva* in the form of a drop on the tip of a blade of grass,
one should grasp it with the *saṃhāra-mudrā*, saying *oṃ huṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ huṃ ātmane namaḥ*, and by means of the *pūraka* breath-retention, establish it within one’s own heart.

Having performed *kumbhaka* (retention), having led [the breath] to one's own *dvādaśānta* by means of the sequence of abandoning the causal deities beginning with Brahmā, and having gathered it back, one should expel it through the right channel (*piṅgalā*).

Having meditated upon the union of the parents, one should simultaneously effect the union of the Self with all wombs in the form of manifold manifestations through the left channel (*iḍā*) by means of the *bhava-mudrā*, reciting: *oṃ huṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ huṃ ātmane namaḥ*. Then, having worshipped and offered three oblations (*āhuti*) with the root mantra, one should make a formal request (*vijñāpya*).

Having offered three oblations with the root mantra and made a formal request for the completion of the entire embryo (*sarvagarbha*), one should contemplate dissolution. Then, having offered three oblations with the root mantra and made a request for the sake of birth (*janana*), one should contemplate dissolution. Having offered three oblations with the root mantra and made a request for the sake of empowerment (*adhikāra*), one should contemplate dissolution. Having offered three oblations with the root mantra and made a request for the sake of enjoyment (*bhoga*), one should contemplate dissolution. Having offered three oblations with the root mantra and made a request for the purification of the streams (*srotas*), one should offer three oblations with the root mantra and make a request for the sake of the non-arising of karma, through the purification of the reality of peace (*śāntitatva*).

Three oblations should be offered to the heart. For the sake of expiation (*niṣkṛti*), having offered one hundred oblations with the *Kavaca* and the preceding *Prāsāda* [mantras], one should inform [the deity]: "O Blessed One, through this expiation of my self, effect the complete purification of all karmas; do so, do so! Then, having visualized the form of exiting from the noose of Mahāmāyā as being free from all impurities, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra. For the purpose of obstructing the impurities, one should offer one hundred oblations with the root mantra.

Therefore, having visualized the separation (*viśleṣa*), one should again offer three oblations with the root mantra. Having contemplated the separation—which consists of the absolute non-existence of impure karma—one should offer three oblations with the root mantra and address [the deity], saying: "O Blessed One, effect the separation of these three bonds (*pāśatraya*) of this self, which consist of the impurity of the authority of Mahāmāyā and impure karma.
Thereafter—
With the *kartarī* [knife] over which the weapon-mantra has been recited seven times—[using] the mantra:

*oṃ hauṃ hyaiṃ hauṃ śāntikalāpāśāya haḥ huṃ phaṭ*—one should cut it at that limit while pronouncing the vowels. Having wiped it with both hands using the weapon-mantra (*astra*), and having rolled it into a circle, one should place it upon the *sūci* [needle] in the *vratapūrṇā* [vessel] along with clarified butter (*ājya*), and burn it by offering it with that same mantra.
"O Blessed One, perform, perform the cutting of the noose of the bundle of fetters of this self," he should thus request.
Again, for the cessation of the sprouts of the fetters, having offered five oblations with the weapon-mantra ending in *huṃ phaṭ*,

and having offered eight oblations with the weapon-mantra for the sake of expiation (*prāyaścitta*), one should contemplate the unity of the remaining body and the consciousness that is free from fetters.

Having invoked and worshipped Īśvara, and having offered an oblation for his presence, one should offer three oblations for the purification of the body of the principles (*tattva-śarīra*) with the mantra: "Oṃ hāṃ, O Īśvara, accept the bride-price (*śulka*) consisting of intellect and ego; svāhā! Then, one should address him thus:
"O Īśvara, bestow upon this traveler a state free from affliction."
"The obstruction must be removed; such is the command of the Supreme Goddess.

Having thus dismissed him, and having meditated upon the Self as standing at the tip of the pure *tattva*, resembling a pure crystal gem and liberated from the net of the *śāntikalā*, he should offer three oblations with the root mantra for the sake of extraction (*uddhāra*).

Having petitioned, "O Blessed One, perform, perform the extraction of this self from the noose of the group of fetters," [the practitioner] extracts the self with the *saṃhāriṇī* [mudrā] and the fierce fire, reciting "oṃ huṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ huṃ ātmane namaḥ," [visualizing it] as resembling a slightly faded moon-maṇḍala during the inhalation (*pūraka*).

Having brought one’s own self into the heart of oneself by means of the *recaka* breath and the *udbhava-mudrā*, and having joined it to the body of the disciple’s thread, one should worship and nourish it... Having sprinkled a drop of *arghya* water on the head of the disciple with the root mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ*, and having offered three oblations (*āhuti*) with the root mantra for the sake of stabilization;
having fully worshipped the two parents and offered three oblations, and having honored them with *arghya*, one should dismiss them with the root mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ*.

"One should offer the full oblation"—this is the purification of the *śāntikalā*. (l. 2) Having uttered the short vowel for the pure *śāntikalā*, one should utter the long vowel for the impure *śāntyatītā*. (l. 3) Then, having worshipped with "Oṃ hyaiṃ hauṃ, obeisance to Śānti and Śāntyatītā" (l. 4), and having offered three oblations while contemplating that the pure has dissolved into the impure, (l. 5) one should re-establish the *śāntyatītā*. Having worshipped in the fire with "Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Ādhāraśakti" (l. 6), one should offer three oblations.
In the body of the Sūtra, having contemplated its pervasion in the station of Śāntyatītā, one should gaze [upon it] with:
*oṃ hauṃ śāntyatītāyai namaḥ*.
Then, for the two principles (*tattva*), [one should recite]: *oṃ hāṃ śaktitattvāya namaḥ* and *śivatattvāya namaḥ*.
Salutation to Nivṛttikalā; salutation to Pratiṣṭhākalā; salutation to Vidyākalā; (l.
2) salutation to Śāntikalā; salutation to Śāntyatītakalā—the five worlds of the Bindukalā.
(l. 3) Salutation to Iṇḍikā; salutation to Dīpirakā; salutation to Rocikā; salutation to Mācikā.

"Salutation to those who move upwards"—thus are the five worlds of the *nādakalā*. "Salutation to Vyomavyāpin; salutation to Vyomarūpa; salutation to Ananta; salutation to Anātha; salutation to Anāśrita"—thus are the five worlds of the *śaktikalā*.

Thus, there are fifteen worlds with names identical to those of the Rudras. Oṃ hāṃ! Homage to the letter *aḥ*. Homage to the letter *aṃ*. Homage to the letter *au*. Homage to the letter *o*. Homage to the letter *ai*. Homage to the letter *e*. Homage to the letter *ḷṛ*. Homage to the letter *ḷṛ*. Homage to the letter *ṛṛ*.

Salutation to the letter *ṛ*. Salutation to the letter *ū*. Salutation to the letter *u*. (l. 3) Salutation to the letter *ī*. Salutation to the letter *i*. Salutation to the letter *ā*. Salutation to the letter *a*—these are the sixteen phonemes. (l. 4) *Oṃ hāṃ oṃ namaḥ*—this is one word. Salutation to Īśāna, the head. (l. 5) *Oṃ haḥ astrāya namaḥ*.

*Oṃ hāṃ hauṃ śivāya namaḥ*—these are the three mantras. *Nādāya namaḥ* and *hakārāya namaḥ*—these are the two seed-syllables (*bīja*). *Kuhvyai namaḥ* and *śaṅkhiṇyai namaḥ*—these are the two channels (*nāḍī*).

"Salutation to Devadatta; salutation to Dhanañjaya"—these are the two [deities] of air (*vāyu*). "Salutation to the organ of speech (*vāgindriya*); salutation to the organ of hearing (*śrotrindriya*)"—these are the two organs (*indriya*).
"Salutation to the object sound (*śabda-viṣaya*)"—this is the object (*viṣaya*).
"Salutation to Dhvaniguṇa"—thus [is] Guṇa.
"Salutation to Sadāśiva-Kāraṇeśvara"—thus [is] Kāraṇeśa.
"Salutation to the state beyond the fourth (turyātītāvasthā)"—thus [is] Avasthā.
"Salutation to the white-colored one"—thus is the color. "Salutation to the circular mandala"—thus is the mandala.
Having thus meditated upon the kalā beyond tranquility (śāntyatīta-kalā) as being encompassed by these [attributes].

Alternatively—having visualized: *oṃ hauṃ, obeisance to the Śāntyatīta-kalā [who is] pregnant with the principles (tattva), worlds (bhuvana), phonemes (varṇa), words (pada), and mantras*—one should strike with a flower below the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*) while reciting: *oṃ hāṃ hauṃ hāṃ śāntyatītakalāyai haḥ huṃ phaṭ*. Then: *oṃ hāṃ hauṃ hāṃ śāntyatītakalāyai namaḥ*.
Thus, with the *rocanaka* [mudrā] and the *udbhava-mudrā*, one should deposit [the deity] into the *kuṇḍa* within the Power (*śakti*) who is the form of the support.

Having worshipped with "Oṃ hāṃ hauṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Kalā Śāntyatītā" and offered the *arghya*, and having offered three oblations for the sake of presence (*sannidhāna*) ending with "svāhā," one should contemplate the three bonds (*pāśatraya*), the office (*adhikāra*), the impurity of karma (*malasuviśuddhakarma*), and the form of Great Māyā.

Having invoked Sadāśiva with "Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Sadāśiva" and worshipped him, one offers three oblations for his presence (*sannidhāna*). Having made the request and visualized the infinite beings of various births within that *kalā*, one worships Vāgīśī and Vāgīśa who pervade it. Having offered an oblation for their presence and prayed for their presence, [one protects] the disciple with the *astra* [mantra].
Having sprinkled [the disciple] with water, one should strike the region of his heart with a flower using the *nārāca-mudrā* while reciting "Oṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ.

Then, entering his body through the syllable *huṃ* by means of one's own exhalation (*recaka*), one should separate [the soul] from him using the *jyeṣṭhā-mudrā* while reciting "Oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ. Next, having drawn it out with the *aṅkuśa-mudrā* while reciting "Oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ svāhā," and while recollecting the root mantra, one should lead it to the *dvādaśānta*.

Having visualized the individual soul (*jīva*) as a drop on the tip of a blade of grass, and having gathered it with the *ātma-mantra* using the *saṃhāra-mudrā*, one should place it within one’s own heart by means of the *pūraka* breath-retention. Having performed *kumbhaka* while recollecting the root mantra, one should lead the soul to one’s own *dvādaśānta* by means of the *ātma-mantra* through the sequence of abandoning the causal deities beginning with Brahmā. Having gathered [the soul] there and contemplated the union of the parents, one should effect the simultaneous conjunction of the self with all wombs in the form of manifold manifestations by means of the *vāmā-udbhava-mudrā*, reciting: *oṃ huṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ huṃ ātmane namaḥ*.

Having worshipped with the root mantra, having offered three [oblations] and made the request; having performed three oblations with the root mantra for the completion of the entire embryo and made the supplication; having offered three oblations with the root mantra for the sake of birth; and having offered three oblations with the root mantra for the sake of authority and made the request.

For the sake of enjoyment (*bhoga*), having offered three oblations with the root mantra and contemplated dissolution (*laya*), one offers three oblations with the root mantra; having made the request for the purification of the channels (*srotas*), one offers three oblations with the root mantra. Having made the request for the purpose of generating the activity (*karman*) and for the purification of the reality beyond peace (*śāntyatītatattva-śuddhi*).

Three oblations should be made with the heart-mantra. For the sake of expiation, having offered one hundred oblations with the root-mantra, and having requested, "O Blessed One, for the sake of my own expiation, perform the purification that brings success in all rites," one should contemplate the separation in the form of emerging from the noose of Mahāmāyā.

Having offered three oblations with the root mantra; having offered one hundred oblations with the root mantra for the purpose of obstructing the impurity of office (*adhikāra-mala*); having contemplated the separation from the impurity of office and offered three oblations with the root mantra; and having contemplated the separation of even pure karma (*śuddha-karma*) in the form of its absolute non-existence and offered three oblations with the root mantra, one should inform the Blessed One: "Perform, perform the separation of the triple bond (*pāśatraya*) consisting of the impurity of office and karma belonging to myself, the Great Illusion (*mahāmāyā*)."

Thereafter, with a blade of kārtrī consecrated seven times with the weapon-mantra *oṃ hauṃ hauṃ hauṃ śāntyatītakalāpāśāya huṃ phaṭ*, one should sever the bond of the *śāntyatīta* kalā at its limit while reciting it with the vowels (*sasvara*), and then burn it. Having wiped [the blade] with both hands using the weapon-mantra and having rounded it, [one should proceed].

Having placed [the offering] into a ladle filled with clarified butter, one should offer it into the fire together with the clarified butter using that very mantra for the purpose of binding. (l. 6) One should then inform [the deity], saying: "O Blessed One, perform the severing of the bonds of the kalās beyond the Śānti [level] for myself. (l. 7) Furthermore, for the cessation of the sprouts of the bonds, one should offer an oblation with the Astra-mantra ending in *huṃ phaṭ*.

Having performed the *pañcaka* rite for the sake of expiation, one should offer eight oblations with the *astra-mantra*. Then, having contemplated the unity of consciousness within the body that has been destroyed by the arrow, one should worship Sadāśiva, the Lord of Causes, with the root mantra. Having offered an oblation for his presence (*sannidhāna*), [one proceeds] for the purification of the *puryaṣṭaka*.

Having offered the bride-price (*śulka*) with three oblations, saying: *Oṃ hāṃ, O Sadāśiva, accept the bride-price consisting of the mind and the drop; svāhā*, he should make this request: "Now, O Bhavodbhava, you who have acted as the maker of the world, having accomplished your task, please out of compassion restrain the individual soul (*aṇu*). Having thus dismissed Sadāśiva, [he proceeds].

Having thus meditated upon the self as being situated at the pinnacle of pure reality, resembling a pure crystal gem and possessing an utterly stainless nature, one should afterwards offer three oblations with the root mantra for the purpose of extraction (*uddhāra*). Having made this request, one should extract the self from the fierce fire of dissolution (*saṃhāriṇī*) by means of [the mantra]: *oṃ huṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ huṃ ātmane namaḥ*.

Having brought oneself, resembling the orb of the autumn moon, into the heart of oneself by means of the inhalation through the left [nostril], and having joined it to the body of the disciple’s thread by means of the exhalation and the *udbhava*-mudrā, one should worship and nourish it; then, having sprinkled a drop of *arghya* water on the head of the disciple with the root mantra, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra for the sake of stabilization.

Thereafter—having worshipped the two parents and offered three oblations—one should inform them on the altar: "For the sake of the disciple's initiation, these two parents have been fashioned by me through compassion; I have honored this station of the Self. Having thus informed them and dismissed them, one should offer the *pūrṇāhuti*. This is the purification of the *śāntyatīta* kalā.

"Oṃ hāṃ hauṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Śāntyatīta and Śakti. Having thus united the pure Śāntyatīta-kalā with the impure power of concealment (*atirodhāna-śakti*) whose form is the crest-tuft (*śikhā*), one should thereafter [unify] the Ātma-tattva, which extends up to the end of the Māyā-tattva, with the mantra: "Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Ātma-tattva."

Having thus performed the ritual attendance (*upasthāpana*) and worship with the root mantra, and having offered one hundred and eight oblations while reciting the commentary for the sake of purifying any deficiency in the ritual procedure, he should perform the ritual attendance and worship of the *vidyā-tattva*—extending to the end of the *māyā-tattva*—with the formula "Oṃ hīṃ, obeisance to the *vidyā-tattva*. Then, for the sake of purifying any deficiency in the mantra, he should offer one hundred and eight oblations while reciting [the mantra] in a whisper (*upāṃśu*).

The Śiva-tattva extends up to the end of the Śakti-tattva. Having presented [the offering] with "Oṃ hūṃ, obeisance to the Śiva-tattva" and having worshipped it while focused in mind, one should offer oblations one hundred and eight times with the root mantra for the purification of mental deficiencies. At this juncture, the teachers maintain that one should offer one hundred oblations with the root mantra for the cessation of the concealer of the power of concealment (*tirodhāna-śakti*).

Then, having visualized the Power (śakti) situated above that [point] as pervading all paths, and having contemplated consciousness (caitanya) at its tip resembling a pure crystal gem, one should cut the topknot with a blade consecrated by that [Power] using the mantra: *oṃ huṃ śikhāyai haḥ huṃ phaṭ*. Then, placing it—wrapped in cow dung and mixed with ghee and honey—into a vessel filled with ghee.

Having offered [the oblation] with "Oṃ hūṃ śikhāyai haḥ hūṃ phaṭ," one should burn it. O Maheśāna, this transgression of the sequence of the womb has been committed by your own will; by your will alone has he crossed over. O Lord of the World, do not cause him to suffer... [End of page 54a, line 1]

"By your will, this purified one shall attain the state of Śiva even through transgression. Having thus informed [the disciple], he should sprinkle him with the *astra-mantra* (*oṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ*). Then, having struck the region of his heart with the *nārāca-mudrā* and flowers while reciting *oṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ*, and having entered his body by means of the *huṃ*-syllable through his own *recaka* breath, he should separate [the disciple's soul] from [his body] using the *jyeṣṭhā-aṅguṣṭha* gesture while reciting: *oṃ haḥ huṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ*.

Having drawn [the soul] out with the mantra *oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ svāhā* while forming the goad mudrā, and having led it to the dvādaśānta, one should contemplate the individual soul (*jīva*) as being in the form of a drop on the tip of a blade of grass; then, seizing it with the *saṃhāra-mudrā* by means of the *ātma-mantra* and bringing it to one's own heart through the process of inhalation (*pūraka*), one should bring about a state of essential identity (*samarasibhāva*) and offer a ladleful of clarified butter (*ājya*).

Having taken up a sacrificial ladle (*sruc*) with its bowl filled and its tip facing downward, adorned with flowers at its top, and held in the *śaṅkha* mudrā, he should rise while recollecting Śiva who pervades all times and paths. Recollecting the flow of the *nāda* within the *suṣumnā* through the unification of the disciple’s self, vital breath, and mind, he should contemplate the disciple’s consciousness as resembling a pure crystal gem.

Uttering the mantra according to the method taught by the Guru, abandoning [the elements] in the sequence of the Lords of the Causes (*kāraṇeśa*), recollecting the Power (*śakti*) and the Drop (*kala*) that have dissolved at the limit, and emitting the stream of all [the elements], one should unite [the self] with Śiva—who is beyond the seventh, who transcends the end, who is at the End of the Twelve (*dvādaśānta*), who is beyond the mind, and in whom the eternal qualities arise devoid of objective existence. For the sake of stabilizing this union, one should again offer the full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*).

Then, having sat down, [one should offer] three oblations of clarified butter with the following three [mantras]: Oṃ hāṃ ātman sarvajño bhava svāhā. Oṃ hīṃ ātman aparitṛpto bhava svāhā. Oṃ huṃ ātman anādibodho bhava svāhā. Oṃ hyaiṃ ātman svatantraḥ bhava svāhā. Oṃ haḥ ātman aluptaśaktir bhava svāhā.

"Oṃ hauṃ! O Self, become possessed of infinite power, svāhā! Having thus bestowed the qualities [upon the deity], one should unite Śiva, who is situated upon the sacrificial mound (*sthaṇḍila*), with [the fire] residing within the hearth, and then dismiss Śiva. Then, having placed Śiva—whose head is turned toward the south—upon the funeral pyre and covered him with a cloth, one should prepare it with fuel and kindle it with the Śiva-fire produced from the center of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*).

Standing at the head of the deceased, having taken up the *sruc* and *sruva* ladles filled with clarified butter, honey, and milk, the preceptor should offer the full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) with the mantra: "O Agni, you are the southern time; the [other] time has not yet arrived. Accept this great oblation, which is joined with the mantras of the *grahas* and is auspicious. Having offered the full oblation, he should cast the *sruc* and *sruva* ladles face down on his left and right sides respectively. In another case, he should simply cast them into the funeral pyre itself.

Then, having performed the auspicious consecration and joined [the cow] with the four [objects], having placed the Vardhanī vessel upon his left shoulder, releasing it as an unbroken stream directed away from him, followed by his kinsmen, he circumambulates it clockwise; then, having set it down facing downward in its proper place and not looking back, he goes to a body of water, spreads *kuśa* grass on the bank, and offers three handfuls of sacrificial food (*nivāpa*).

*Oṃ hāṃ, O pure self, become Īśa, svadhā! Oṃ hāṃ, O pure self, become Sadāśiva, svadhā! Oṃ hāṃ, O pure self, become Śānta, svadhā!* Having offered [these mantras] and bathed again, those who carry the corpse on their shoulders and the one who cremates it should each recite the *Saṃhitā* or the *Aghora* mantra one hundred times, while the others recite it twice that amount. Those unrelated [to the deceased], having placed the shoulder-bearer upon the ground, [should offer] barley into the fire.

Having bathed and recited [the mantra] two hundred times, one should bathe again and worship Īśvara. A twice-born man who has observed his vows must not follow one who is deficient in an ear. Having followed him and bathed in water, he should recite the mantra of his own clan-god one hundred times. Whether he was observing a vow or not, if he carries a deceased Brāhmaṇa initiated into Śiva, there shall be no untimely death for him. [Likewise, if he carries] a Śiva-yogin who has passed away, being alone and without a protector...

He who, having brought [the body] back, performs the consecration (*saṃskāra*), is not afflicted by misfortunes. Then, having brought the funeral lamentation, having arrived at the door of the house, having buried *nimba* leaves, and having touched earth, fire, water, cow-dung, and white mustard seeds, and having placed a stone at the foot [of the threshold], they should enter the house; and for the sake of the Self and for the sake of the Immortal, they should offer to the God food brought by others—consisting of flavorful, wholesome, and life-sustaining items—in the afternoon.

Now, regarding the specific procedure for the initiation of the deceased (*mṛtakadīkṣā*): (l. 7) For one who desires the initiation into *nirvāṇa*, the initiation must be performed upon the very body of the deceased who has passed away in his presence. (l. 8) Even in the case of one who has died in another region, or who had already received initiation, or even if no funeral rites (*antyeṣṭi*) have been performed for him, (l. 9) one should fashion a representative image (*pratikṛti*). (p. 57a, l. 1) By means of *darbha* grass, or with flour mixed with cow-dung and the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*), having fashioned the image, (l. 2) one should cut it as before, preceded by the ritual of the weapon (*astrakaraṇa*), and thus complete the sacrifice.

Having placed a small vessel containing the five products of the cow and auspicious water near the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) to his right, he should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*), preceded by the utterance of the heart-seed syllable (*hṛdbīja*), upon the locations of the subtle body, the principles (*tattvas*), their presiding deities, and their respective lords, using *karavīra*, *arka*, and lotus flowers.

"Salutation to Rodha-śakti at the *brahmarandhra*," and so on; having thus mentally projected [the elements] from the end of the earth-element down to the hells and the netherworlds (*pātāla*), and having worshipped them with scents and other offerings, one should meditate upon their form. Then, within the pericarp of the heart-lotus, there are three channels (*nāḍī*) known as Piṅgalā, Iḍā, and Suṣumṇā, located in the left, right, and middle [respectively].

In those [fires], having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of the triad of powers—Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, and Raudrī—as well as *dharma* and *adharma*, and having invoked and established the Self within the self by means of the "Great Net" (*mahājāla*) application, one should perform the rites up to the "joining" (*yojanī*) as before and burn [the body] as before. At the conclusion of that burning, having offered three oblations to the Self-principle (*tattvātman*) and dismissed the fire, one should collect the ashes and cast them into deep water.
Thus [it is stated] in the *Svāyambhuva*.
Even for one who has died in a foreign land, the funeral rites (*antyeṣṭi*) for the initiated must indeed be performed;
at that time, having fashioned an image even with *kuśa* grass,
it should be done with cow dung mixed with milk, or with *kuśa* grass alone.
For one who has died without having performed the final rite (*iṣṭi*), the Guru, having fashioned a representative image (*pratikṛti*), completes the procedure for initiation for the deceased.
The ritual for initiation for the deceased is concluded.
Initiation for the deceased refers to [the case of] an untimely death.
Now, [the merit] of those whose lives have been taken by negligence, by thieves, fire, or weapons; or of those killed by elephants, tigers, rivers, snakes, or in battle.
Having extracted [the soul] from others who are devoid of self and have pierced their own souls,
one should first burn even their bodies with the fire of Śiva’s mantra.
Having recited the Aghora mantra one hundred thousand times, one should offer the Rudra-bali as prescribed.
In the Rudra-region, one should worship the Rudras; which Kṣetrapālas should one name?
Those Rudras who perform fierce deeds, whose actions are terrible, and who dwell in fearsome abodes;
and those others, the guardians of the fields (*kṣetrapālas*), as well as the *piśācas*, *dānavas*, and so forth.
May all the well-proportioned [deities] accept this offering (bali),
which has attained the state of a Piśāca through the power of Ugratūrya.
Having requested, "Release [them]," one should cast forth the *bali* offering for nourishment.

The application of the mantras for worship, the offering of the *bali*, and so forth is as follows: "Oṃ hāṃ! Salutation to Rudra, Raudra, Kṣetrapāla, Piśāca, Rākṣasa, Dānava, Bhūta, Graha, Kūrma, and the others, including the *balika*s and so on. Svāhā! (P. 58b, l. 1).
Having bathed and returned, he should feed four or eight ascetics who observe the great vow (*mahāvrata*), such as the Pāśupatas and others;
having satisfied them with garments and sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*), he should dismiss them.
Having fashioned a circular form out of *darbha* grass as a likeness of that body,
and having drawn it upon a cloth, bound it, and adorned it;
having performed the remaining rites as previously described, one should join it to the stainless seat.

Thus ends the exposition of the rite for the final sacrifice (*antyeṣṭi*) for those whose selves have reached every state, according to various established doctrines and reasonings by the venerable Aghoraśambhu.
Now follows the final sacrifice accompanied by the purification of the *kalās*, performed either simultaneously or in sequence.

As before, up to the joining of the channels (*nāḍīsandhāna*), one should wash the ritual thread (*apāśasūtra*)—which has ceased its activity—and the *kartarī* (scissors), then sprinkle them, encircle them with the sacred thread (*avakuṇṭhya*), scatter [offerings] over them, and bind them to the crest-lock (*śikhā*) with the root mantra.

Having drawn [the soul] from that body into the *suṣumnā*, having joined it to the thread, having veiled it, and having prepared it with three oblations (*āhuti*), one should take the power (*śakti*) from the disciple’s head, place it upon the thread, and cause it to become present there with three oblations. Having entered his heart, separated [the soul], and gathered it, one should establish it in one's own heart and lead it to the *dvādaśānta*. Having gathered it there—

Having brought [the thread] to the middle of the eyebrows, drawn it out, joined it to the thread, and enveloped it, one should satisfy it with oblations. Then, having taken up the three bonds of impurity (*mala*), action (*karman*), and illusion (*māyā*), as well as the power of obstruction (*rodha-śakti*), and having joined them to that which resides in the thread, one should satisfy each with oblations and observe the *nivṛtti* [kalā].

"Oṃ hlāṃ, obeisance to the Nivṛtti-kalā who contains within her the elements, worlds, phonemes, words, and mantras"—having thus struck below the knees, gathered [the thread], joined it to the cord, worshipped it, enveloped it, and gratified it with oblations, one should gaze upon the Pratiṣṭhā-kalā below the navel.

"Oṃ hvīṃ, salutation to the *pratiṣṭhā*-kalā, which contains within it the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), and mantras"—having thus struck [the thread], joined it to the cord, made it present with oblations (*āhuti*), and looked at it below the throat, [he recites]: "Oṃ hrūṃ, [salutation] to that which contains within it the principles, worlds, phonemes, words, and mantras..."

Having struck [the thread] with "Obeisance to Vidyākalā," having taken it up, having joined it to the thread, and having enveloped it with oblations, one should cause her to be present. Having beheld Śāntikalā below the midpoint of the eyebrows, [one recites]: "Oṃ hyaiṃ, obeisance to Śāntikalā, who contains within her the principles (tattva), worlds (bhuvana), phonemes (varṇa), words (pada), and mantras."

Thus, having struck [it], taken it up, joined it with the thread, and veiled it, and having gratified it with oblations; having beheld the Śāntyatītā [kalā] below the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra), [one should say]: "Oṃ hauṃ, obeisance to the Śāntyatītā who contains within her the principles (tattva), worlds (bhuvana), phonemes (varṇa), words (pada), and mantras. Having thus struck [it] and taken it up, [one places it] upon the thread.

Having joined [the disciple] and honored him with oblations, and having brought him into proximity; likewise, having recalled the lineage, lifespan, enjoyments, and other pledges (*samaya*) of the disciple, as well as his conduct and the karma and impurities within him; and having performed the rites of satiation (*tarpaṇa*) and illumination (*dīpana*); and having applied marks of saffron and so forth upon the locations beginning with the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*).

Having worshipped Śiva together with his limbs (*sāṅga*) therein, one should tie a knot in the thread with the mantra: *oṃ hauṃ hlāṃ hvīṃ hrūṃ hyaiṃ hauṃ hauṃ bhahavann nivṛtti-pratiṣṭhā-vidyā-śānti-śāntyatītā-pāśān-mala-karma-māyā-śakti-tattva-bhuvanāni vyāpakaṃ bandha bandha huṃ phaṭ*.

Then, having worshipped the Support Power (*ādhāraśakti*) in the fire and gratified her with oblations, [one should contemplate] the *nivṛtti*-kalā located below the knees within the differentiation of the thread of the disciple’s body; it consists of the earth-element, the phonemes, the letters, the *ajaha* mantra, the worlds contained within time, the word beginning with *oṃ* and ending with the state of being, the lotus, karma, and accompanied by *māyā*.
